overview: This Senate resolution names September 2025 "National Literacy Month." It points to national and international test results showing that many students and adults read at low levels, and notes that weak reading skills are tied to lower graduation and employment rates. It highlights the "science of reading," a body of research behind teaching methods such as phonics, vocabulary and comprehension practice. The resolution asks governments, schools, libraries, nonprofits, businesses and the public to mark the month with programs and activities. It does not create new programs or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 16, 2025.
for: Supporters say putting a national spotlight on reading encourages schools and communities to adopt proven teaching methods and helps the many adults and children who struggle to read.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it doesn't change any law, add funding for literacy programs, or require any school to change how it teaches reading.
